title: Comments Threading + Mentions — Data Model & API Refinement
description:
## Parent Ideation Context
- Title: Threaded Replies + @Mentions for Article Comments
- Version: 6

### Description
Feature ideation for pulse-brownfield-feature-demo. Context: `app/` is a fresh fork of nsidnev/fastapi-realworld-example-app (FastAPI + Postgres RealWorld/Conduit clone), documented in `app/FORK_NOTES.md`. Auth/error conventions are documented in `docs/decisions/0001-token-auth-scheme.md`. This board was reset (prior ideation/refinement/spec/sprint/card chains hard-deleted) so this pipeline can be authored fresh and handed off pre-validation for a live walkthrough.

### Problem Statement
The forked RealWorld app (nsidnev/fastapi-realworld-example-app, upstream commit 029eb7781c60d5f563ee8990a0cbfb79b244538c) models article comments as a flat, unordered list: each comment belongs to an article and an author only (see `app/db/repositories/commentaries.py` and the `commentaries` table), with no reply-to relationship and no way to tag another user inside a comment body. This blocks two concrete user needs: (1) replying to a specific existing comment so a conversation reads as a thread instead of a flat wall, and (2) @mentioning another user by username inside a comment so they can be made aware they were referenced. Neither capability exists today in the fork.

### Proposed Approach
Extend the comments domain rather than introducing a new entity, to stay consistent with the existing RealWorld data model:

1. **Threading** — add a nullable self-referential `parent_comment_id` (FK to `commentaries.id`, same article) to the comment record. A comment with `parent_comment_id = null` is top-level; non-null makes it a reply. Depth is limited to one level (replies-to-top-level-comments only, no reply-to-reply nesting) — mirrors lightweight threading (e.g. GitHub PR review threads) rather than arbitrary-depth nesting.
2. **@Mentions** — parse the comment body for `@username` tokens at write time, resolve each against existing registered usernames (case-sensitive exact match, consistent with existing username lookups elsewhere in the fork), and persist resolved mentions as first-class records (`comment_id`, `mentioned_user_id`) rather than leaving them as unstructured text. Unresolved `@token`s are left as plain text, not linked, and do not error the request.
3. **API surface** — extend the existing comment create/response schema with `parent_comment_id` (optional on create, present on read) and a `mentions` array (username + user id) on the read response. Existing flat-list comment endpoints keep working unchanged for clients that ignore the new fields.
4. **Auth & error conventions** — all new/changed endpoints follow ADR 0001 (`Token` auth scheme, not `Bearer`; flat `{"errors": [...]}` error shape). E.g. replying to a nonexistent `parent_comment_id`, or replying to a comment on a different article than the URL's, returns a business-rule error via the existing flat-array shape.
5. **Notification delivery** — explicitly out of scope. `mentions` are persisted and readable via the API; active notification (email/in-app/websocket) is a separate concern for later.

Explicit stated assumptions (not left as silent ambiguity), carried forward unchanged from this feature's original scoping session with the user, which already confirmed this exact scope: one-level-deep threading only; mentions require an exact, case-sensitive existing username; unresolved mentions are silently left as plain text; no notification delivery in this pass.

### Scope Assessment
- Domains: 2/5
- Ambiguity: 2/5
- Dependencies: 1/5
- Complexity: medium
in_scope: ["Add nullable self-referential parent_comment_id (INTEGER, FK to commentaries.id, ON DELETE CASCADE) to the commentaries table via a new Alembic migration following the fdf8821871d7_main_tables.py create_*_table() convention", "Add a new comment_mentions table (comment_id FK->commentaries.id ON DELETE CASCADE, mentioned_user_id FK->users.id ON DELETE CASCADE) with a composite uniqueness constraint on (comment_id, mentioned_user_id)", "Extend CommentInCreate schema with optional parent_comment_id: Optional[int]", "Extend Comment domain model + response schema with parent_comment_id: Optional[int] and mentions: List[MentionedUser] (username + id)", "Validate on create: parent_comment_id must reference an existing comment on the SAME article, and that parent comment must itself be top-level (parent_comment_id IS NULL) to enforce one-level-deep threading", "Parse @username tokens from comment body at create time via regex, batch-resolve against users.username with exact case-sensitive match (reusing UsersRepository's existing lookup pattern), persist matches to comment_mentions", "Unresolved @tokens (no matching username) remain as plain text in body, are not persisted to comment_mentions, and do not error the request", "GET /articles/{slug}/comments and POST /articles/{slug}/comments both return parentCommentId and mentions on every comment in the response", "All new business-rule errors (nonexistent parent_comment_id, cross-article parent, reply-to-a-reply) use the existing flat {\"errors\": [...]} shape via the existing HTTPException/http_error_handler path"]
out_of_scope: ["Reply-to-reply / arbitrary-depth nesting \u2014 explicitly one level only per ideation assumption", "Active notification delivery (email/in-app/websocket) when mentioned \u2014 mentions are persisted and readable via API only", "Case-insensitive or fuzzy username matching for mentions", "Editing an existing comment to add/remove parent_comment_id or mentions after creation \u2014 no PATCH/PUT endpoint exists for comments today and none is being added", "Any frontend/UI work \u2014 this fork has no frontend component"]
analysis:
**Source code (fork at `app/`, upstream commit 029eb7781c60d5f563ee8990a0cbfb79b244538c):**

- `app/db/migrations/versions/fdf8821871d7_main_tables.py:167-194` — `create_commentaries_table()` defines the current schema: `commentaries(id, body, author_id FK->users.id ON DELETE CASCADE, article_id FK->articles.id ON DELETE CASCADE, created_at, updated_at)`. No self-reference, no mentions table. The file's per-table `create_*_table()` helper-function convention (one function per table, called from `upgrade()`) is the pattern a new migration must follow.
- `app/db/queries/sql/comments.sql:20-34` — aiosql-style named queries. `create-new-comment<!` does `WITH users_subquery AS (SELECT id, username FROM users WHERE username = :author_username) INSERT INTO commentaries (...) RETURNING ...` — confirms username lookup is exact-string `WHERE username = :value`, no case-insensitive collation, matching the case-sensitive-mention assumption.
- `app/db/repositories/comments.py:61-78` — `CommentsRepository.create_comment_for_article()` is the single write path for comment creation; calls `queries.create_new_comment` and maps the row via `_get_comment_from_db_record` (line 87). Any `parent_comment_id`/mention handling must be added here.
- `app/models/domain/comments.py:6-8` — `Comment(IDModelMixin, DateTimeModelMixin, RWModel)` has only `body: str` and `author: Profile`. No `parent_comment_id` or `mentions` field exists.
- `app/models/schemas/comments.py:15-16` — `CommentInCreate(RWSchema)` has only `body: str`. This is the request schema `POST /articles/{slug}/comments` binds to (via `app/api/routes/comments.py:47`, `Body(..., embed=True, alias="comment")`).
- `app/api/routes/comments.py:26-57` — `list_comments_for_article` (GET) and `create_comment_for_article` (POST) are the two endpoints in scope. Both depend on `get_repository(CommentsRepository)`. No route changes needed beyond schema fields — routing/dependency wiring stays the same.
- `app/db/repositories/users.py:17-26` — `UsersRepository.get_user_by_username()` is the existing exact-match username lookup pattern; mention resolution should reuse this same repository rather than a bespoke query.
- `app/api/errors/http_error.py:6-7` — confirms `{"errors": [exc.detail]}` flat-array shape for all `HTTPException`s (business-rule errors). Matches ADR 0001.

**Knowledge Graph (Stage 2 query set, run before this refinement moved to approved):** `okto_pulse_kg_find_similar_decisions` (topic: comment threading data model / mention resolution) returned 0 hits; `okto_pulse_kg_find_contradictions` (board-wide, no existing decisions to anchor on) returned 0 pairs. `okto_pulse_kg_list_alternatives` not applicable — no existing decision node to query alternatives for; this refinement is the first decision recorded on this board (the board was reset — see ideation description). No prior art to extend or contradict.

**Web research:** not required — no third-party library/protocol dependency is introduced (Alembic and aiosql are already in use and unchanged in usage pattern).

**Stakeholder context:** the exact scope (one-level threading, case-sensitive exact-match mentions, no notification delivery) was already explicitly stated as assumptions in the parent ideation and is carried forward unchanged; no open Q&A exists on the ideation.
decisions: ["Extend the existing commentaries table with a nullable self-referential FK rather than introducing a separate threads/replies entity \u2014 matches the existing RealWorld data model's convention of flat tables with FKs (see favorites, articles_to_tags as precedent for join-table style) and requires no new domain concept. No prior KG decision exists to extend or supersede (board reset, zero prior nodes) \u2014 this is new knowledge, not a reuse.", "Depth-limit enforcement (one level only) happens at the repository/service layer on create, not as a DB CHECK constraint \u2014 consistent with how the existing codebase validates business rules in Python (e.g. comment-author-matches-check in check_comment_modification_permissions) rather than in SQL constraints, and keeps the error message flowing through the existing flat-array HTTPException path instead of a raw asyncpg constraint-violation error.", "Mentions persist as a separate comment_mentions join table rather than a JSON/array column on commentaries \u2014 enables a straightforward FK to users.id (referential integrity, cascade delete) and a simple indexed lookup, matching the existing join-table pattern (favorites, articles_to_tags, followers_to_followings) already established in fdf8821871d7_main_tables.py."]
